groups.canonical: For each request, a pulse or flash is required before the next stop; the no-stop case and response-step inclusivity are unspecified.
groups.explanation: These statements give the same request/deadline obligation without deciding vacuity or same-step responses. Explicit no-stop, strict-after and inclusive variants remain separate.

members.text: Whenever a request occurs, a pulse or a flash must occur before the next stop occurs.
For each request, before any subsequent stop, a pulse or flash must take place.
For every request, a pulse or a flash occurs before the next stop.
For every request, before the next stop after it, a pulse or a flash must occur.

groups.canonical: Each request receives a pulse or flash at the request step or later, before the next stop.
groups.explanation: The same-step allowance is explicit here and is not added to statements leaving that boundary unresolved.

members.text: Each request is followed by a pulse or flash before the next stop, at the same step or later

groups.canonical: Each request needs a pulse or flash before a subsequent stop if one occurs; no response is required when no subsequent stop occurs.
groups.explanation: Both make the stop condition conditional and preserve no-stop vacuity without demanding a stop.

members.text: Every request receives a pulse or flash before the next stop, if a next stop occurs; no stop is necessarily required.
For every request, a pulse or a flash occurs before any subsequent stop; if no stop occurs, there is no requirement.

groups.canonical: For each request followed by a stop, a pulse or flash must occur strictly after the request and before the next stop.
groups.explanation: This explicitly excludes a same-step response and makes the obligation conditional on a later stop.

members.text: For every request, if a stop occurs afterward, a pulse or a flash occurs after the request and before that next stop.

groups.canonical: A request still requires an eventual pulse or flash when no next stop occurs.
groups.explanation: This independently stated no-stop obligation is stronger than the conditional/vacuous alternatives and is retained as the original whole statement.

members.text: If there is no next stop, the pulse or flash is still eventually required by the request.

groups.canonical: The state remains active until a release occurs, with release eventuality unspecified.
groups.explanation: The unqualified until statement is not assigned a mandatory-release or optional-release interpretation.

members.text: The state must remain active until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: The state remains active until a release, with whether release must occur left unresolved or not explicitly required.
groups.explanation: The originals leave release necessity unresolved: required versus optional, may or may not be required, or not explicitly required. None is promoted to a positive forever-without-release assertion.

members.text: The state is active at every step until a release occurs, with a release required or optional
The state remains active until a release occurs; release may or may not be required.
The state remains active continuously until a release occurs; the release is not explicitly required to occur.

groups.canonical: The state remains active until a release that must eventually occur.
groups.explanation: The release is expressly mandatory.

members.text: The state stays active until a mandatory release occurs.

groups.canonical: The state remains active until an optional release; without a release it stays active forever.
groups.explanation: These positively assert optional release or perpetual activity without release; mere absence of an explicit release requirement remains in the unresolved-necessity group.

members.text: The state stays active until a release occurs, release being optional.
From now until the first release, the state is active; if no release occurs, the state stays active forever.

groups.canonical: The state is active at every step before a release.
groups.explanation: The original is phrased only over the pre-release interval and does not resolve release occurrence or the absent-release case.

members.text: The state is active at every step before a release.

groups.canonical: From some relevant point the state remains active until a release.
groups.explanation: The onset is an unspecified relevant point rather than expressly now.

members.text: From some relevant point, the state remains active until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: If no release occurs, the state remains active forever.
groups.explanation: This is the original no-release conditional clause, not a full independently asserted release-case obligation.

members.text: If no release occurs, the state remains active forever.

groups.canonical: Every request requires the state to be active from that request step until a release.
groups.explanation: The same request-step onset is explicit; eventual release and endpoint activity remain unspecified.

members.text: Whenever a request occurs, the state must remain active from that step until a release occurs.
Whenever a request occurs, the state is active from that step until a release occurs
Whenever a request occurs, the state remains active from that request onward until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: Every request requires the state to be active until a release, without an explicit activation-step boundary.
groups.explanation: The original omits the explicit from-that-step qualifier retained in the preceding group.

members.text: Every request requires the state to be active until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: For every request, the state is active until release; release is optional and absence of release leaves it active forever.
groups.explanation: These give the optional-release or unless-released interpretation of the request obligation.

members.text: For every request, the state is active from the request step until a release occurs; if no release occurs, it stays active forever.
For every request, the state is active until the next release; release is optional.
For every request, the state remains active unless or until release.

groups.canonical: For each request at step t, activity may begin at t or later and continue until release.
groups.explanation: Allowing delayed activation is weaker than requiring activation at the request step.

members.text: For every request at step t, the state must remain active from t or a later step until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: Each request creates an active-state obligation ending at release, possibly requiring eventual release.
groups.explanation: The original leaves an eventual-release alternative open and is kept whole.

members.text: Each request creates an active-state obligation that ends at a release, possibly requiring eventual release.

groups.canonical: Eventually a starting point is reached from which the state stays active until release, with release eventuality unspecified.
groups.explanation: These use an eventual or existential onset and leave release occurrence unresolved.

members.text: Eventually, a step is reached from which the state remains active until a release occurs.
Eventually the state is active continuously until a release occurs
There exists a step N such that from N onward the state remains active until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: At some future point the state stays active until release, with release eventuality unspecified.
groups.explanation: These expressly locate the onset at a future point; no optional-release or forever clause is added.

members.text: At some future point, the state stays active until a release occurs.
At some future point the state is active until release.

groups.canonical: From a future point the state stays active until an optional release; absent release it stays active forever.
groups.explanation: Both explicitly allow the release to be absent.

members.text: From some future point, the state remains active until a release occurs; the release may be absent.
There is a future step from which the state stays active until a release occurs; if no release occurs, it stays active forever.

groups.canonical: Eventually the state becomes active and stays active until an optional release.
groups.explanation: This expressly describes becoming active and optional termination; its onset wording is retained rather than replaced by the strict-future wording.

members.text: Eventually the state becomes active and remains active until a release; release is optional.

groups.canonical: Before an onset N the state may be inactive; after N it becomes active and stays active until release.
groups.explanation: The before/after N wording and absence of a release-eventuality decision are preserved.

members.text: Before N the state may be inactive; after N it becomes active and stays active until release.

groups.canonical: Starting at every step, the state must stay active until a release occurs.
groups.explanation: All have the globally renewed every-step obligation without resolving whether releases must occur.

members.text: At every step, the state must remain active until a release occurs.
From any time step onward, the state must stay active until a release happens.
At every step, the state is active until a release occurs

groups.canonical: Starting at every step the state stays active until release, described as continuous activity unless released.
groups.explanation: The original includes an explanatory unless-released characterization; it is kept whole rather than equated to a one-time obligation.

members.text: Starting at every step, the state remains active until a release occurs, effectively requiring it to stay active continuously unless released.

groups.canonical: From every step the active-until-release obligation holds with release optional; if none occurs activity persists forever.
groups.explanation: All retain the every-step scope and optional-release behavior.

members.text: At every step, the state is active from that step until a release occurs; if no release occurs, it stays active forever.
From any point, the state remains active until release; release is optional.
The obligation to stay active until release holds globally from every step, implying permanent activity if no release occurs.

groups.canonical: The state is always active unless or until a release occurs.
groups.explanation: This can describe one activity obligation ending at release, unlike an obligation explicitly renewed at every later step.

members.text: The state is always active unless or until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: At every step the state must be active and remain active until release.
groups.explanation: The explicit every-step activity assertion is retained separately from until statements that can leave activity at the release step open.

members.text: At every step, the state must be active and remain active until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: The state remains active and the indicator lit continuously until release, with release eventuality unspecified.
groups.explanation: These share conjunction throughout the interval and do not decide optional versus mandatory release.

members.text: Both the state must be active and the indicator lit until a release occurs.
The state remains active and the indicator lit continuously until a release happens.
The state and the indicator are both lit and active continuously until a release occurs
The state remains active and the indicator remains lit throughout the interval until a release occurs.
The state remains active and the indicator remains lit until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: From now until an optional release, both the state is active and the indicator lit.
groups.explanation: Release is explicitly optional, unlike the unresolved until statements.

members.text: From now until a release, both the state is active and the indicator is lit; release is optional.

groups.canonical: Both conditions hold until release, with release possibly required.
groups.explanation: The eventual-release possibility is retained as part of this whole original rather than split into separate votes.

members.text: Until release, the state is active and the indicator is lit; release may be required.

groups.canonical: Both conditions hold at every step before a release.
groups.explanation: The original explicitly describes the pre-release interval without resolving the absence of release.

members.text: Both conditions hold at every step before a release.

groups.canonical: If no release occurs, both the state stays active and the indicator stays lit forever.
groups.explanation: This original states the no-release conditional, not a complete positive release-case obligation.

members.text: If no release occurs, the state remains active and the indicator remains lit forever.

groups.canonical: The state stays active until the first release or cancellation; either event can end the obligation.
groups.explanation: All give the same alternative termination condition without expressly requiring an eventual terminating event.

members.text: The state must remain active until either a release occurs or a cancellation occurs.
The state stays active until the first occurrence of a release or cancellation.
The state is active until either a release or a cancellation occurs
The state remains active until either a release or a cancellation occurs; either terminating event may end the obligation.
The state is active until the first of release or cancellation; either event can end it.
The state remains active until the first of a release or a cancellation occurs.

groups.canonical: The state remains active until an optional release or cancellation, and stays active forever if neither occurs.
groups.explanation: The unless-until and explicit absent-termination statements share optional termination.

members.text: The state is active until either a release or a cancellation occurs; if neither occurs, it stays active forever.
The state remains active unless or until release or cancellation.

groups.canonical: Either release or cancellation ends the active-state obligation; neither event is explicitly required.
groups.explanation: The original focuses on alternative optional termination and is retained as its own whole explanatory statement.

members.text: Either a release or a cancellation ends the active-state obligation; neither event is explicitly required.

groups.canonical: The state remains active until a release coincides with the indicator being lit.
groups.explanation: These locate the lit-indicator condition at the terminating release rather than throughout the preceding interval.

members.text: The state must remain active until a step occurs where both a release occurs and the indicator is lit.
The state stays active until a release happens while the indicator is lit.
The state is active until a release, and the indicator is lit at the release step
The state is active until a release, and at that release step the indicator is lit.
The state is active until a release that occurs while the indicator is lit.
The state remains active until a release occurs at a step when the indicator is lit.

groups.canonical: The state stays active until release and the indicator stays lit throughout that interval.
groups.explanation: These extend the lit-indicator condition over the waiting interval.

members.text: The state is active until a release occurs, with the indicator lit throughout that interval
The state is active until a release occurs, and the indicator is lit during that interval.

groups.canonical: The state stays active until release with the indicator lit during the interval, while also leaving a release-coincidence reading possible.
groups.explanation: This single original explicitly combines alternative scopes and must not be split into independent votes for either narrower interpretation.

members.text: The state remains active until a release occurs, and the indicator is lit during that interval; the wording may also mean the release-period state must coincide with a lit indicator.

groups.canonical: The terminating release must coincide with the indicator being lit.
groups.explanation: This original only constrains the terminating event; it does not independently assert the state-active prefix and is therefore not merged with full active-until-release interpretations.

members.text: The terminating release must coincide with the indicator being lit.

groups.canonical: The state stays active until a point from which the indicator remains lit permanently; activity is no longer required after that endpoint.
groups.explanation: These share permanent illumination as the termination condition and do not expressly require that endpoint to arrive.

members.text: The state must remain active until a point from which the indicator stays lit permanently.
The state is active until the indicator enters a permanently lit condition.
The state stays active until the indicator becomes lit permanently
The state is active until a point from which the indicator is lit forever; after that point there is no requirement.
The state remains active until the indicator is permanently on.
The state remains active until a point from which the indicator stays lit forever.

groups.canonical: The state remains active until the indicator becomes permanently lit, and that endpoint eventually occurs.
groups.explanation: The original explicitly says the permanent-lit condition eventually serves as the endpoint.

members.text: The state remains active until the indicator becomes permanently lit; the permanent-lit condition eventually serves as the endpoint.

groups.canonical: The state stays active until permanent illumination; if that never happens, it stays active forever.
groups.explanation: This explicitly preserves the absent-endpoint case as perpetual activity.

members.text: The state is active until the indicator becomes permanently lit; if that never happens, the state stays active forever.

groups.canonical: Permanent illumination of the indicator ends the active-state obligation.
groups.explanation: This original states the termination effect without independently asserting the full preceding activity interval.

members.text: Permanent illumination of the indicator ends the active-state obligation.

groups.canonical: Every request starts an active-until-release obligation at the immediately following step.
groups.explanation: All retain exact next-step onset and a release cutoff, without resolving release eventuality.

members.text: Whenever a request occurs, starting at the next step the state must remain active until a release occurs.
After any request, the state must be active from the next step until a release.
After each request, starting at the next step, the state stays active until a release occurs
Whenever a request occurs, beginning at the next step the state remains active until a release occurs.
For every request, from the next step onward the state is active until a release occurs.
For every request at step t, the state must remain active starting at step t plus one until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: Every request starts activity at the next step until an optional release; without release activity persists forever.
groups.explanation: Both explicitly resolve release as optional while preserving exact next-step onset.

members.text: For every request, from the step after the request until a release, the state is active; release is optional.
For every request, the state is active starting at the next step until release; if no release occurs, it stays active forever.

groups.canonical: A request does not require activity at its own step; activity is required only from the next step onward.
groups.explanation: The original states a request-step exemption and next-step onset but omits the release cutoff, so it is retained separately from full active-until-release obligations.

members.text: The request itself does not require the state to be active at the request step, only from the next step onward.

groups.canonical: Before the first release, every pulse requires a flash at the immediately next step; the trigger obligation ends at release.
groups.explanation: All preserve the pre-release pulse scope and exact next-step flash. Ending the trigger interval does not remove a flash already required by a prior pulse.

members.text: Before any release occurs, every pulse must be followed by a flash at the next step.
Until a release happens, any pulse must have a flash at the immediately following step.
Until a release occurs, every pulse is followed by a flash at the next step
Until a release occurs, every pulse is followed by a flash exactly at the next step.
Before the first release, every pulse has a flash at the immediately following step.
Until a release occurs, every pulse is followed by a flash at the next step; after release there is no requirement.
Before any release, a pulse implies a flash at the next step.
Before the first release, every pulse must be followed by a flash exactly at the next step.

groups.canonical: After release the pulse-to-next-step-flash obligation no longer applies.
groups.explanation: This is the original post-release exemption alone, not another assertion of the full pre-release rule.

members.text: After the release occurs, the pulse-to-next-step-flash obligation no longer applies.

groups.canonical: The first state stays active until handoff starts a second active-state phase that eventually ends at a required release.
groups.explanation: These give the same ordered two-phase obligation and explicitly require the release ending the second phase.

members.text: The first state must remain active until a handoff occurs, after which the second state remains active until a mandatory release ends it.
The first state stays active until a handoff, after which the second state stays active until a release, and the release must eventually occur
The first state remains active until a handoff; after the handoff, the second state remains active until a release, which must eventually end that second phase.
The first state is active until a handoff, then the second state is active until release; release is required to end the second phase.
The first state remains active until a handoff occurs; after the handoff, the second state remains active until a release, and that release must eventually occur.
The behavior is a two-phase sequence: first-state active, handoff, second-state active, mandatory release.

groups.canonical: The first state stays active until handoff, then the second state stays active until release, without an explicit eventual-release requirement.
groups.explanation: The original does not retain the mandatory-release qualifier present in the other two-phase statements.

members.text: The first state stays active until a handoff, which starts a phase where the second state stays active until a release occurs.

members.text: The first state is active until a handoff; after the handoff the second state is active until a release; a release eventually occurs.

groups.canonical: A handoff transitions from first-state activity to second-state activity, and a release eventually ends the second phase.
groups.explanation: This transition-and-termination statement does not independently require continuous first-state activity before handoff, unlike the full two-phase prefix obligations.

members.text: A handoff transitions from first state active to second state active, and a release eventually ends the second phase.

groups.canonical: A handoff eventually occurs with the first state active beforehand; from the handoff onward the second state stays active until release, with release eventuality unspecified.
groups.explanation: Both explicitly start the second-state obligation at the handoff. After/then onset and explicitly possibly-required release alternatives remain separate.

members.text: A handoff must eventually occur, with the first state active before it; from the handoff onward the second state remains active until a release occurs.
A handoff must eventually occur, with the first state active before it; from the handoff onward, the second state remains active until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: A handoff eventually occurs with the first state active up to it; the second is active from handoff until release.

members.text: A handoff must eventually occur with the first state active up to that handoff, and from that handoff the second state must remain active until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: A handoff eventually occurs while the first state is active; afterward the second is active until release.
groups.explanation: The first-state condition is simultaneous with handoff, rather than expressly beforehand.

members.text: Eventually a handoff occurs while the first state is active; after it the second state is active until a release occurs.

groups.canonical: A handoff is mandatory, starts the second-state obligation, and an eventual release ends that obligation.
groups.explanation: Eventual release is explicitly mandatory here.

members.text: The handoff is mandatory, the second state obligation starts at the handoff, and a release eventually ends it.

groups.canonical: A handoff eventually occurs with the first state active beforehand; afterward the second state stays active until release, with exact handoff-step onset unspecified.
groups.explanation: After-handoff or then wording is retained separately from explicit from-the-handoff inclusive onset. Release eventuality is not resolved.

members.text: Eventually a handoff occurs preceded by the first state being active, after which the second state stays active until a release.
A handoff must eventually occur with the first state active before it, and after the handoff the second state stays active until a release
There is a future handoff preceded by the first state being active, then the second state is active until release.

groups.canonical: A handoff eventually occurs with the first state active beforehand; from handoff the second state is active until release, and release may be required.
groups.explanation: The original explicitly leaves a required-release alternative open. That unresolved combined interpretation stays whole and separate from statements that do not explicitly articulate the alternative.

members.text: Eventually a handoff occurs with the first state active beforehand; from that handoff the second state is active until release, and release may be required.

groups.canonical: Every pulse must have a flash at some strictly later step, including the immediately next step as a possible delay.

members.text: Whenever a pulse occurs, a flash must occur at a strictly later step.

For every pulse, a flash occurs at some strictly later step.
For every pulse, a flash occurs at the next step or later.
For every pulse, a flash occurs later, not at the same step.
Whenever a pulse occurs, a flash must occur at some strictly later step.

groups.canonical: A pulse must be followed at a subsequent time by a flash, with quantification over pulses not made explicit.

members.text: A pulse must be followed at some subsequent time by a flash.

groups.canonical: Every pulse is followed later by a flash with at least one step separating the events.

members.text: There exists a pulse that is followed later by a flash.

After a pulse, beginning at the next step, the light remains on forever.
For every pulse, from the step after the pulse onward the light is on forever.
For every pulse, from the next step onward the light stays on.
After any pulse, the light is on permanently starting at the next step.
Whenever a pulse occurs at step t, the light is on for every step after t and remains on forever.

Whenever a pulse occurs, there is some later step from which the light becomes on and remains on forever.

members.text: The required order is pulse, then flash, then chime.

Whenever a pulse occurs while the enable state holds, a flash must occur at some strictly later step.
Only enabled pulses create a later-flash obligation; disabled pulses are unconstrained.

groups.canonical: Every pulse before the first stop requires a flash strictly after that pulse and strictly before that first stop.
groups.explanation: These keep the first-stop scope and the flash strictly inside the pulse-to-stop interval.

members.text: For any pulse occurring before the first stop, a flash must occur strictly after that pulse and also strictly before that first stop.
Before the first stop occurs, any pulse must be followed by a flash that also precedes that stop.
Any pulse before the first stop is followed by a flash at a later step that also occurs before that stop
For every pulse before the first stop, a later flash occurs before that first stop; the flash must be strictly later than the pulse.
For every pulse before the first stop, a flash occurs later than the pulse and before the first stop.
For every pulse before the first stop, a flash occurs later and also before that stop.
For every pulse before the first stop, a flash must occur later than the pulse but before that first stop.

groups.canonical: Before any stop, every pulse requires a later flash before that stop.
groups.explanation: The any-stop scope can include pulse/stop intervals after the first stop and is not silently restricted to the first-stop prefix.

members.text: Before any stop, every pulse has a later flash before that stop.

groups.canonical: The required flash must occur strictly between the pulse and the first stop.
groups.explanation: The original states endpoint ordering alone and does not independently quantify over every pulse before the first stop, so it is separate from the full trigger obligation.

members.text: The required flash must be strictly between the pulse and the first stop.
